cells.tense: You are standing in what patience grew, and you can tell its worth.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Pick a debt you carry with somebody — a word, a hand, a borrowed object — and clear it this week before they ask. Quiet is fine.
cells.core:
Somebody can be near you and still be told the truth about what is owed between you. That is the harder half of closeness and you have it: near enough to hurt, honest enough to count. People leave your company settled rather than spun, and they usually cannot say what you did.

What the slow work grew is in now, so check it with your own hand. A word owed, a hand owed, a thing you borrowed — clear it before anyone comes asking. Nobody needs to watch you do it. That is the inner sense of what's right deciding a small case, and after a while the case stops feeling small.
cells.sheetLine: You can stay close and still keep a fair count.
cells.verb: gather and weigh what the slow work has grown, and keep what holds
cells.place: close enough to feel with someone, without fusing with them

cells.tense: The harvest is coming in early, and nothing in it has finished growing.
cells.act: let the feeling settle into its own depth
cells.ask: Give one evening to whatever you're closest to. No fixing, no next step, no reading of where it stands.
cells.core:
Lately you have been reading the yield before it is in: testing the ties, tallying what people give, deciding the future of a closeness that is still growing. It looks like care. Up close it lands as a verdict handed down over a season that isn't finished.

The heart already knows who matters; it does not need another audit. Give an evening to the tie that matters most and do nothing with it — no fixing, no next step, no reading of where it stands. What is solid will be solid after the evening. The counting has been standing in for something; sit with the thing itself and see what shows up.

cells.tense: The harvest came in, and you stayed indoors while it did.
cells.act: find the rhythm and stay in it
cells.ask: Reach toward somebody you still have, at a size you could keep for a month. Then keep that size, whatever the first answer is.
cells.core:
Feeling with people still runs in you, but it is not reaching anyone lately. What grew between you and somebody got no gathering and no weighing, and the chances for it closed quietly while no decision was being made.

Closeness does not come back through one big push; it comes back at a pace you can hold past a week. Reach toward somebody you still have at a size you could keep for a month — a short call, a walk, a line written — and keep that size whatever the first answer is. The tie does not need the missing time made up in a single day, and steady will read truer to it than rescued.

cells.tense: You have been setting the order of the tie and calling it nobody's doing.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: To the one you're closest to, state where the two of you stand and what you're holding. Once, plainly, no case built after — then stop talking.
cells.core:
The order of the ties you are in has been yours to set. You decide the pace, decide what this is between the two of you and what it isn't, and later it reads as just how things went. It holds because you made it. The other person is living inside something nobody has said out loud.

So say it out loud. To the one you're closest to, state where the two of you stand and what you're holding — once, plainly, no case built after it, then stop talking. That is not a demand. It puts the frame where they can see it and answer it, and afterward the two of you are in the same picture instead of one of you holding it privately.
cells.sheetLine: You've set the order here and called it luck.
